decisions.executionNote: Holder is in the right workspace and pens on the left. Begin turning right gripper inward for a side grasp, retaining elbow-up continuity.
Approach holder from its right side with open jaws, continuing the inward rotation in small increments.
Align open right fingers around the holder rim/body. Final approach is slow; grasp depth remains visually estimated.
Close right gripper around the holder, then make a short vertical test lift. Check RGB for retention before moving pens.
Holder rose with the right hand. Raise it to loading height while bringing the left arm upward and forward toward the nearer cyan marker.
Keep the holder steady. Move the open left gripper above the left cyan marker while completing its downward approach orientation.
Align left fingers across the cyan marker near its cap. Approach above the table with a near-vertical gripper; right hand remains fixed.
Fine-align and lower left fingertips onto the cyan marker, then close. Confirm retention with a subsequent lift.
Lift the closed left gripper away from the tabletop, then begin turning the retained marker upright. Keep the holder fixed.
Marker is retained. Turn it upright while lifting and approaching the holder from the left; maintain clearance above its rim.
Replan from the interrupted pose with much smaller rotation increments. Translate the upright marker over the holder without crossing the arm links.
Lower the first upright marker into the opening, correcting slightly left to clear the rim. Both grips remain closed during insertion.
Release the marker inside the holder, then withdraw left and upward. Observe whether it settles upright before the next pickup.
First marker is visibly seated. Turn the left gripper toward the yellow-and-black pen while remaining high above it.
Complete the downward orientation and approach the yellow pen near its capped end. Keep a small vertical clearance before closing.
Lower onto the upper barrel of the yellow pen and close the left gripper. Keep the holder stationary.
Allow the left fingers to finish closing, then make a small lift to test retention of the yellow pen.
Yellow pen is visibly retained. Lift and retreat slightly left while beginning its upright rotation, keeping clear of the holder.
Continue rotating the yellow pen upright at a safe height to the left of the holder. Keep both grasps closed.
Bring the upright yellow pen over the holder from the left, slowing rotation near the final orientation. Preserve clearance above the rim.
Finish straightening the yellow pen and align its lower end with open space beside the first marker. Begin a slow insertion.
Lower the yellow pen farther into the holder and open the left fingers to let it settle. Right hand keeps the holder supported.
Withdraw the open left gripper clear of the yellow pen. Move toward the remaining cyan marker while checking both inserted pens stay in the holder.
Two pens are visibly seated. Turn the left fingers to match the remaining cyan marker and approach it from above.
The previous approach was rejected without motion. Retry the same alignment with substantially smaller increments to preserve joint continuity.
Continue the now-continuous left-arm approach, rotating downward and translating toward the cyan marker cap.
Complete the downward orientation and move above the remaining cyan marker's capped end, leaving clearance for visual correction.
The forward approach reached a continuity limit. Retract and lower the left wrist while rotating more slowly, restoring reach margin before approaching again.
Approach the cyan marker again from the lower, retracted configuration and finish aligning the fingers across its barrel.
Use a forward-tilted grasp rather than extending the wrist farther. Lower and tilt gradually to reach the marker while preserving elbow configuration.
The tilted open fingers appear table-limited. Back away and change to a shallow approach along the marker length, keeping the closing direction horizontal.
Set a moderate angled grasp along the marker length, lowering slowly with horizontal jaw closure to avoid table contact.
Fine-adjust the angled grasp across the cyan marker, close the left fingers, and hold still before testing retention.
Test the cyan marker grasp by lifting while retracting the left wrist, preserving reach margin. Keep the holder steady.
The angled grasp retained the marker. Lift and retract while rotating its capped end upward; adapt to its actual orientation rather than a standard grasp.
Finish bringing the cyan marker upright and move toward the opening from the left, with its lower end still clear of the rim.
Translate the upright cyan marker over the holder's remaining space and lower toward the rim. Keep the angled wrist orientation unchanged.
Lower the third marker into the available opening and release it, keeping the holder supported and watching for interference with the seated pens.
Withdraw the open left fingers from the crowded holder to let the third marker settle; do not push farther against the seated pens.
The third marker fell onto the table beside the holder. Retract and reorient the left gripper for a new top-down pickup in its closer location.
Continue reorienting toward a top-down grasp of the fallen marker while keeping the left hand clear of the held cup.
Approach the fallen marker from directly above, completing the downward orientation and stopping short of tabletop contact.
Shift along the fallen marker toward its middle, lower gently, and close the left fingers for a straighter recovery grasp.
Lift the recovered marker vertically, then retract leftward to clear the holder before turning it upright.
The recovered cyan marker is retained. Lift it clear of the holder and turn its capped end upward with a controlled retracted motion.
Bring the recovered marker upright above the left side of the opening, slowing the last part of rotation. Keep its lower end clear until aligned.
Replan after the continuity interruption with smaller rotations. Align the recovered marker over the opening and approach the rim slowly.
Move the recovered marker slightly deeper across the opening while lowering it gradually, avoiding the near rim and the two seated pens.
The recovered marker's lower end now appears inside the holder. Release and withdraw gently left/up to let it settle without catching the rim.
Three pens are now visible in the holder. Move the open left gripper toward the remaining black pen, starting a downward grasp orientation.
Retry after the zero-motion continuity rejection with smaller increments, moving left and gradually turning toward the last pen.
Continue downwards toward the black pen's upper barrel, with the fingers open and the holder supported.
Finish the vertical approach to the black pen, keeping the jaws across its barrel and stopping just above the table.
Close around the black pen and make a short vertical test lift. Keep the filled holder steady in the right hand.
The black pen is retained. Raise and turn it upright while approaching the holder from the left with ample rim clearance.
Continue straightening the last pen above the holder. Use smaller rotation increments near the upright configuration.
Finish straightening the black pen and lower its end toward the remaining opening, using small increments to preserve continuity.
Lower the black pen into the holder and release it gently. Keep the right hand fixed until the final pen settles.
Withdraw the left hand from the four pens, then begin lowering the supported holder toward the table without changing its orientation.
All four pens remain visible in the holder. Lower it toward the tabletop while retracting the empty left arm toward its starting configuration.
The holder appears at tabletop height. Lower a final few millimeters, release it slowly, and continue returning the left arm toward its start.
Withdraw the open right gripper from the placed holder, while completing the left arm's return to its original pose. Check that the filled holder stays upright.

Complete the right arm's return to its starting pose. Both grippers are open, and the filled holder remains upright on the table.
